title: Closed finite exceptional adjoint and counit on classical inputs
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$. Work with ordinary sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A$ on the small etale and pro-etale sites and their ordinary derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $
u_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}	o T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and $D^+$ for objects with cohomology vanishing sufficiently far below. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, with quasi-compact complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $c=(\operatorname{id}_Z,i)$ be the compactification of $i$, and let $i_c^	imes$ be the ordinary etale right adjoint of $Ri_!^c$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Let $i_{\mathrm{supp}}^	imes$ be the right adjoint of termwise $i_*$ on $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ in [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle]. There is a canonical natural isomorphism $Ri_!^c\cong Ri_{\mathrm{et},*}\cong i_*$ on the whole unbounded ordinary etale derived category. The resulting unique right-adjoint isomorphism $i_c^	imes\cong i_{\mathrm{supp}}^	imes$ identifies their counits.

For every $B\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, put $D=i_{\mathrm{supp}}^	imes B$ and $K=
u_X^*B$. Then $D$ is bounded below and there is a natural isomorphism
$$Ri^!K=
u_Z^*i_c^	imes R
u_{X,*}
u_X^*B\xrightarrow{\sim}
u_Z^*D.$$
Here $Ri^!$ is exactly the finite transported exceptional functor of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Under $
u_X^*i_*D\cong i_*
u_Z^*D$, its counit on this classical input is the $
u_X^*$-image of the etale closed-support counit $i_*D	o B$. No constructibility assumption is imposed.

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian (its ideals are $0$ and $k$), and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X,Z$ Noetherian. On ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves, [lem-trf-oriented-closed-base-localization] gives exact closed direct image $F=i_{\mathrm{et},*}$. By [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], its total unbounded right derived functor is canonically its termwise descent: an exact functor preserves kernels, images and hence cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms. The localization universal property [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] identifies this descent with the total right derived functor: its comparison is already invertible before any resolution, and natural transformations out of either functor are the same transformations after localization. For $c=(\operatorname{id}_Z,i)$, [def-amb-etale-compact-support] gives $Ri_!^c=Ri_{\mathrm{et},*}D(\operatorname{id}_!)$. The presheaf formula in [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] at the identity is already the given sheaf, so its sheafification and derived descent are identities. This gives the asserted canonical isomorphisms on the entire unbounded etale category. In the rest of the proof read the compact-support adjunction through this left-functor isomorphism.

proof.text: Write $G=i_c^\times$, $J=i_{\mathrm{supp}}^\times$, and write $\epsilon^G:FG\to1$ for the compact-support counit after Step 1. The support adjunction $F\dashv J$ and its counit $\epsilon^J$ are those of [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle]. Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] to these two adjunctions of the same unbounded etale functor $F$. It gives a unique natural isomorphism $\gamma:G\xrightarrow{\sim}J$ characterized, for every $M$, by $\epsilon^J_M\circ F(\gamma_M)=\epsilon^G_M$. This proves the first right-adjoint and counit assertion without restricting to constructible or bounded objects.

proof.text: Choose $a$ with $B\in D^{\ge a}$. Exactness of $F$ in Step 1 makes $F$ t-exact, since $H^m(FV)=F(H^mV)$ termwise. Put $T=\tau_{\le a-1}(JB)$ using the standard truncation of [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Then $FT\in D^{\le a-1}$, so the orthogonality axiom of [def-weil-t-structure] gives $\operatorname{Hom}(FT,B)=0$. Under $F\dashv J$, this is $\operatorname{Hom}(T,JB)=0$. In particular the truncation map $T\to JB$ is zero. In degrees $m<a$ it induces an isomorphism on cohomology, by the explicit kernel truncation, so $H^m(JB)=0$. Thus $D=JB\in D^{\ge a}$; this is a direct truncation argument on the unbounded category, without a cohomological-dimension assumption.

The last bijection is comparison full faithfulness in [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]; the value is bounded below by the finite definition [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Expanding these adjunction bijections, the inverse image of the identity of $

$$r_B\circ\epsilon^G_{R
u_{X,*}K}=\epsilon^G_B\circ FG(r_B)=\epsilon^J_B\circ F(\gamma_B)\circ FG(r_B)=\epsilon^J_B\circ F( eta_B).$$
Substitute in Step 5 and use naturality of $\lambda$ at $ eta_B:E	o D$:
$$\epsilon^{\mathrm{tr}}_K=
u_X^*(\epsilon^J_B)\circ
u_X^*F( eta_B)\circ\lambda_E^{-1}=

Thus after identifying $Ri^!K$ with $
u_Z^*D$ by $\alpha_B$ and identifying $
u_X^*i_*D$ with $i_*
u_Z^*D$ by $\lambda_D$, its counit is exactly the image of the etale support counit. The equation uses the actual comparison unit and counit and is natural in $B$; every object to which comparison full faithfulness was applied is bounded below by Steps 3--4.
